extraction.name: OpenThoughts3
extraction.description: A dataset for training reasoning models, focusing on math, code, and science.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The OpenThoughts project creates open-source datasets for training reasoning models by exploring the design space of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) datasets, focusing on identifying the best questions and corresponding answers that encourage reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper discusses various strategies for handling missing data, including verification and filtering methods.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is collected from various sources including StackExchange, CodeForces, OpenR1, and others.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The project involves multiple generations of releases, starting with BespokeStratos-17K and progressing through OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, and culminating in OpenThoughts3-1.2M.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: The paper discusses experiments on data imputation and filtering, including response length filtering and difficulty-based filtering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is manipulated through various stages including question sourcing, mixing questions, question filtering, deduplication, sampling multiple answers per question, and answer filtering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing involves filtering out low-quality questions and answers, deduplication, and sampling multiple answers per question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The data annotation involves generating answers using a teacher model, and verifying answers through various methods including LLM-based verification and majority consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotation platform used includes GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-R1, and QwQ-32B.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses analysis of annotations, including considerations related to converting raw annotations into final labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset includes 16 human labels per dataset item.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The demographics of annotators include various researchers and contributors to the OpenThoughts project.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The machine annotation tools used include GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-R1, and QwQ-32B.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released under Apache 2.0 license and is available on openthoughts.ai.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain sensitive human attributes such as math, code, and science questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The project aims to demystify the SFT data curation process and gain a deeper understanding of what contributes to a strong reasoning SFT dataset.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses potential biases in the dataset, including limitations and non-recommended uses.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations, including not exploring datasets for reinforcement learning, and not exploring the use of staged SFT or curriculum learning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning reasoning models.
